descriptionChirho: Active correction or punitive discipline administered by a superior (God or parent) to bring about obedience, expressed in the Piel stem across all inflections.
To impart knowledge or skill through guided instruction, emphasizing education rather than punishment, in Qal and Piel stems.
Passive reception of disciplinary correction, indicating the subject undergoes or accepts chastisement, in the Nifal stem.
Reflexive sense of heeding a warning or learning a cautionary lesson, often as an exhortation to accept correction before punishment comes.
Active verbal correction or reproof in the Qal stem, emphasizing the role of the one who admonishes or corrects others.
Causative chastisement with connotation of binding or restraining, as in the Hifil usage in Hosea where discipline involves physical constraint.
